content: Magnesium hydroxide, when administered within 4 hours of levofloxacin, reduces the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to use caution, monitor the patient, and separate the administration of these drugs by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both drugs. Caution is advised, and administration should be separated by 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of lisdexamfetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of lisinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of memantine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of methscopolamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and administration should be separated by 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For extended-release methylphenidate capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), which are pH-dependent, coadministration with antacids or acid suppressants may alter drug release. Consider separating the administration of antacids and methylphenidate extended-release capsules to avoid this interaction. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Separate antacid and neratinib dosing by at least 3 hours. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours before or 2 hours after nilotinib. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Magnesium decreases serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. Use alternatives if available. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide through fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide through fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Vitamin D increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by raising serum magnesium concentrations, particularly in the presence of renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Vitamin D increases the levels of aluminum hydroxide by promoting aluminum retention, which may lead to toxicity. Avoid coadministration. Caution is advised, and administration should be separated by 2 hours. Amikacin decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. Separate dosing by at least 2 hours between antacids and acalabrutinib. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of atenolol by inhibiting GI absorption.
